title: Galaxy Surfactants Hits Upper Circuit as Q1 Profit More Than Doubles
excerpt: The specialty chemicals maker's shares surged 20% to a 52-week high of Rs 2,508 after reporting a 109% jump in net profit to Rs 165.9 crore on record quarterly EBITDA.
body:
• Galaxy Surfactants shares surged 20% to hit a 52-week high of Rs 2,508.40 on the NSE after Q1 FY27 results showed net profit jumping 108.7% year-on-year to Rs 165.9 crore.
  • Revenue rose 38.5% YoY to Rs 1,785.2 crore, while quarterly EBITDA hit a record Rs 252.5 crore on healthy volume growth.
  • The stock has gained roughly 30% over the past month, recovering sharply from its 52-week low of Rs 1,510 hit in late March.
  • Motilal Oswal has a buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 3,160.

Galaxy Surfactants Ltd, one of India's leading manufacturers of performance surfactants and specialty care ingredients, saw its shares lock in at the 20% upper circuit limit on August 14 after reporting a blowout set of quarterly results that far exceeded market expectations.

The Numbers Behind the Surge

The company's Q1 FY27 results, announced after market hours on August 13, showed net profit soaring 108.7% year-on-year to Rs 165.9 crore, more than doubling from the year-ago quarter. Revenue climbed 38.5% to Rs 1,785.2 crore, while EBITDA hit a record Rs 252.5 crore for the quarter, driven by healthy volume growth across all geographies and segments.

"Revenue climbed 38.5% to Rs 1,785.2 crore, while EBITDA hit a record Rs 252.5 crore for the quarter, driven by healthy volume growth across all geographies and segments."

The scale of the beat was significant. The stock opened at Rs 2,412.50 on Thursday and immediately surged to Rs 2,508.40, hitting its 52-week high and locking at the upper circuit — the maximum permissible daily gain of 20% from its previous close of Rs 2,090.40.

A Turnaround Story

The results mark a decisive turn for Galaxy Surfactants, which had spent much of the past two years navigating weak demand and an industry-wide inventory destocking cycle that weighed on specialty chemicals makers globally. The stock had fallen to a 52-week low of Rs 1,510 in late March 2026 before beginning its recovery.

The company, which manufactures over 215 product grades for the home and personal care industry and serves more than 1,500 clients worldwide, has operations spanning India, the United States, and Egypt. Its products are used as key ingredients in shampoos, detergents, soaps, and other personal care and cleaning products.

Galaxy Surfactants' managing director K. Natarajan has previously noted visible signs of improving demand for premium specialties, suggesting the volume momentum should be sustained going ahead. The company had guided for 6-8% volume growth and EBITDA per ton of Rs 20,500-21,500 for the fiscal year.

Analyst View

Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintains a buy rating on Galaxy Surfactants with a target price of Rs 3,160, implying further upside from current levels. The brokerage had flagged the company's results as beating estimates significantly in recent quarters, with net profit coming in 20% above projections.

At the upper circuit price, Galaxy Surfactants commands a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 7,244 crore, with a trailing P/E ratio of about 27.7. Promoters hold a 70.9% stake, with foreign institutional investors at 4% and domestic institutional investors at 1.5%.

What's Next

The sharp Q1 beat suggests Galaxy Surfactants may be entering a new earnings upcycle as demand normalises across geographies. With record EBITDA, accelerating volume growth, and a lean balance sheet (debt-to-equity of just 0.09), the company is positioned to benefit from any sustained recovery in global personal care and home care spending. Investors will be watching whether the volume momentum persists in coming quarters and whether margins continue to expand.
